question: Which normalized vectors describe the same pure qubit state, and what can one computational-basis probability pair establish?
entry: Exact prerequisite2.2: complex inner products, normalization and Cauchy–Schwarz equality; computational-basis ket notation and physical postulates introduced locally.
exit: State pure-state and fixed-basis Born postulates; derive probability normalization and global-phase invariance; compare vectors with phase alignment without equating one probability pair with a state.
assumptions: Ideal pure qubit represented in a fixed orthonormal computational basis
Unit complex vectors modulo a common unit-modulus scalar
Computational-basis Born probability rule; no general measurement/update postulate imported
Phase alignment exact derivation uses normalized finite-dimensional inner products; numerical execution has explicit1e-12 absolute tolerance

symbols.alpha,beta: Complex amplitudes in the fixed basis
symbols.u,theta: Global unit-modulus scalar and its real phase angle
symbols.a,b,c,z: Unit coordinate vectors, conjugated overlap and aligning scalar
